text:
Corn's water requirement depends heavily on when in the season it is planted. Based on research for Battambang and Kampong Cham provinces (Vance et al. 2004), the estimated total rainfall needed across the growing season is:
- Early wet season, planted in April: 340-480 mm
- Early wet season, planted in May: 420-600 mm
- Wet season, planted in July-August: 560-690 mm

Rainfall in Cambodia's corn-growing areas typically increases through the early wet season and peaks around July-September. Because reliable germination generally needs at least about 50 mm of rain to wet the soil profile adequately, the probability of reaching this threshold varies by month and province: in Battambang and Kampong Cham, the chance of reaching 50 mm rainfall is roughly 20-40% in March, 60-70% in April, and about 90% by May. Farmers are advised to wait until soil moisture is adequate before planting in the early wet season, since planting too early -- ahead of reliable rains -- raises the risk of poor or failed establishment.
